bug_semantics: NLTK's AllowlistUnpickler (nltk/picklesec.py) validates only the pickle's module string (prefix allowlist via _module_allowed: module == name or module.startswith(name + ".")) and NEVER the global name against the allowlist. find_class then resolves whatever (module, name) pair passes via super().find_class, which for pickle protocol >= 4 resolves dotted names by getattr-chaining. Consequence: with e.g. sklearn allowlisted, an untrusted pickle requesting global 'sklearn.os.system' traverses attributes to reach os.system and executes — arbitrary command execution. Prefix entries also expose every attribute of every module in the namespace (dunders like __builtins__/__loader__, re-exports, in-namespace gadget callables such as numpy.f2py.crackfortran.myeval and nltk.tokenize.repp.ReppTokenizer._execute). Attack vector: crafted untrusted transition-parser model loaded by TransitionParser.parse through allowlisted_pickle_load (CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data).
flaw_origin: Commit f26b3753038d937b68145daf15e9636f8451053c ("fix(security): prevent pickle RCE in TransitionParser model loading (CWE-502) (#3631)", 2026-07-01, author Litesh Ghute, committer GitHub) added class AllowlistUnpickler to nltk/picklesec.py with find_class checking `(module, name) in self._allowed_globals or self._module_allowed(module)` and _module_allowed doing the prefix match on module only — the name-agnostic check and the attribute-traversal gap are both born here (the class docstring even claims "os.system ... can never be reconstructed", the promise the bypass breaks). Parent 8493007b3e has picklesec.py without AllowlistUnpickler (only RestrictedUnpickler/WarningUnpickler from 5c56f229f5a7, 2025-12-15 Eric Kafe, which raised on ALL globals and had no allowlist to bypass).
